transcript.content: Hello. I'm glad you're here today. What brings you in to see me?

Once I start eating in the evenings, it feels like I can’t stop or control it at all. It has gotten to the point where it feels completely out of hand, and a close friend finally urged me to come in and get some help.
After these episodes where you feel you can't stop eating, do you ever try to prevent weight gain by making yourself throw up, using laxatives, fasting, or exercising excessively?

Yes, I do, and I feel so ashamed about it. Lately, I've been making myself throw up until my throat burns or taking laxatives before bed because I can't stand the thought of all that food staying inside me. Other times, I force myself to go on long, punishing walks after my shift and skip meals the next day to try and make up for it.
How often do these episodes of overeating and purging occur, and for how many months has this been happening?
It happens several nights a week, usually right after I finish my shift at work. This whole pattern of losing control and then trying to undo it has been going on for about six months now.
How do you feel about your body shape and weight, and would you say you have an intense fear of gaining weight or becoming fat?

I am absolutely terrified of gaining weight, and I judge my entire worth by how flat my stomach looks in the mirror each morning. If I see even a tiny bit of softness or if the scale goes up by a single pound, I panic and feel like a complete failure. It completely ruins my day until I can find a way to undo it.
To help me better understand your physical health, could you share your current height and weight, and let me know if you have experienced any major weight changes recently?

I don't actually know my exact weight or height off the top of my head. To be honest, I try to avoid looking at the scale entirely because seeing the numbers just causes me too much panic and distress.
Could you describe what and how much food you typically eat during one of these evening episodes where you feel you've lost control?

I usually just stand at my kitchen counter and eat a massive amount of food in less than an hour, even if I wasn't even hungry. I'll go through half a loaf of bread with peanut butter, a frozen pizza, leftover takeout, and whatever snacks I can find. It's so humiliating because I just can't seem to stop myself once I start.
Even if you don't know the exact numbers, would you say your current weight is generally considered underweight, normal weight, or overweight, and have you recently lost a large amount of weight?

I'm not really sure what category my weight falls into, or if I've lost a large amount of weight recently. I just know that I am constantly terrified of gaining anything, and when I look in the mirror, I feel absolutely huge.
Have family, friends, or doctors ever expressed concern that you are too thin or underweight, even if you feel otherwise?

No, nobody has ever expressed concern that I'm too thin or underweight. A close friend of mine was really worried, but that was because she knew my eating habits were getting completely out of control, not because of my weight.
If you menstruate, have your periods stopped or become very irregular since these eating patterns started?
I haven't really noticed any major changes to my period. They still seem to be pretty regular, even with everything else going on.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient meets all diagnostic criteria for Bulimia Nervosa (F50.2). She reports recurrent episodes of binge eating characterized by consuming large amounts of food in a short period with a subjective loss of control. To prevent weight gain, she engages in recurrent inappropriate compensatory behaviors, including self-induced vomiting, laxative misuse, fasting, and excessive exercise. These episodes have occurred several times a week for six months. Her self-evaluation is unduly influenced by body shape and weight, and she exhibits an intense dread of fatness. She does not meet the weight criteria for Anorexia Nervosa, as she has regular menses and no reports of being significantly underweight.
